settings_help.source: (bool) - Run Cellpose segmentation for every configured object channel (cell, nucleus, pathogen, organelle) and write each object's labels into fov.ome.zarr (labels/<object> of each field; masks/<object>_mask_stack/*.npy for 'npy', 'tiff' and timelapse runs). False performs preprocessing only, producing normalized arrays without label masks; downstream measurement therefore requires a subsequent segmentation step. Default True.

(bool) - Keep the run's working masks/ folders after every field is merged. Off by default: they are removed once each field is committed to fov.ome.zarr (or merged/ for 'npy' and timelapse runs), which holds the channels and every mask. With fov.ome.zarr every segmentation stage writes its masks straight into the field's labels (no masks/<object>_mask_stack folder); kept, those labels are reused by a rerun, otherwise a rerun segments again. With fov.ome.zarr no stack/ folder is written at all: preprocessing stores each field's channels straight into fov.ome.zarr. Older projects' stack/ folders are still read, and kept or removed by this setting as before.

(str) - Where Mask Generation keeps the fields Measure reads. 'ome-zarr' writes each field straight into fov.ome.zarr in the project folder: preprocessing stores the acquired channels there (no stack/ folder), and every segmentation stage writes its masks as the field's label images (no masks/<object>_mask_stack folder); one OME-Zarr plate store (row/column/field), the channels in their acquired dtype, one shard file per field image and per label image; no merged/*.npy is written. 'npy' writes stack/*.npy and merged/*.npy as before. 'tiff' writes merged/*.npy plus merged_tiff/<field>.tif and <field>_<object>_mask.tif. Timelapse runs always write stack/ and merged/*.npy, because the plate store has no time axis yet. Older projects with stack/, masks/<object>_mask_stack, merged/*.npy or images/<plate>.ome.zarr still read. Default 'ome-zarr'. Alpha.
